questions.question_english: A highly sought-after private school in Delhi receives 500 applications for 100 entry-level seats. The Principal decides to interview parents to assess their educational background before finalizing the lottery pool. Does this violate the RTE Act?
options_english: Yes. Interviewing parents is a prohibited screening procedure.
No. Parent interviews are valid if the final allocation is made by lottery.
Only if the school also charges a capitation fee.
No. The screening prohibition applies only to government schools.
questions.explanation_english: Yes, because interviewing parents constitutes a prohibited screening procedure. Section 2(o) defines a screening procedure as any method of selection other than random selection. Section 13 explicitly prohibits subjecting children or parents to interviews or tests during admission. Interviewing parents to filter or select applicants violates statutory mandates, requiring schools to utilize non-discriminatory, random selection processes like open lotteries for entry seats.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर विकल्प A है। धारा 13 प्रवेश की स्क्रीनिंग प्रक्रिया पर रोक लगाती है। माता-पिता का साक्षात्कार बच्चे की पृष्ठभूमि के आधार पर गैर-यादृच्छिक चयन करने का साधन बन सकता है; बाद में लॉटरी कराने से पहले किया गया ऐसा साक्षात्कार वैध नहीं हो जाता। यह रोक केवल सरकारी विद्यालयों तक सीमित नहीं है और कैपिटेशन फीस लेने की अलग घटना होना भी आवश्यक नहीं है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) Yes. Interviewing parents is a prohibited screening procedure.

Yes, because interviewing parents constitutes a prohibited screening procedure. Section 2(o) defines a screening procedure as any method of selection other than random selection. I. सोसाइटी फॉर अनएडेड प्राइवेट स्कूल्स ऑफ राजस्थान बनाम भारत संघ (2012) ने गैर-अल्पसंख्यक निजी गैर-सहायता-प्राप्त विद्यालयों के लिए धारा 12(1)(ग) की संवैधानिक वैधता को स्वीकार किया।
II. प्रमति एजुकेशनल एंड कल्चरल ट्रस्ट बनाम भारत संघ (2014) ने अल्पसंख्यक शैक्षणिक संस्थाओं को RTE अधिनियम के दायरे से छूट दी।
III. एनवायरनमेंटल एंड कंज़्यूमर प्रोटेक्शन फाउंडेशन बनाम दिल्ली प्रशासन का मामला मुख्यतः पेयजल और शौचालय जैसी बुनियादी विद्यालयी सुविधाओं से संबंधित था।
कौन-से कथन सही हैं?
options_hindi: केवल I और II
केवल II और III
केवल I और III
I, II और III

questions.question_english:
Consider the following landmark Supreme Court decisions related to the RTE Act:
I. Society for Unaided Private Schools of Rajasthan v. Union of India (2012) upheld the constitutional validity of the Act, including Section 12(1)(c) for private unaided non-minority schools.
II. Pramati Educational and Cultural Trust v. Union of India (2014) exempted minority educational institutions from the purview of the RTE Act.
III. Environmental & Consumer Protection Foundation v. Delhi Administration concerned basic school infrastructure, including drinking water and toilets. Which statements are correct?
options_english: I and II only
II and III only
I and III only
I, II and III
questions.explanation_english: Landmark judicial rulings shaped RTE implementation: the 2012 Society for Unaided Private Schools judgment upheld Section 12(1) (c) for private non-minority schools; the 2014 Pramati decision exempted minority institutions; and the Environmental & Consumer Protection Foundation case mandated basic drinking water and functional toilet infrastructure across all schools.
questions.explanation_hindi: स्रोत की उत्तर-कुंजी के अनुसार सही उत्तर I, II और III है। सोसाइटी फॉर अनएडेड प्राइवेट स्कूल्स मामले (2012) में गैर-अल्पसंख्यक निजी गैर-सहायता-प्राप्त विद्यालयों पर 25% प्रवेश प्रावधान लागू होने की संवैधानिक वैधता को बरकरार रखा गया। प्रमति निर्णय (2014) ने अल्पसंख्यक संस्थाओं के संदर्भ में RTE की प्रयोज्यता पर निर्णय दिया। पर्यावरण एवं उपभोक्ता संरक्षण फाउंडेशन से संबंधित मुकदमा विद्यालयों में आधारभूत सुविधाओं, जैसे पेयजल और शौचालय, से जुड़ा था।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (D) I, II and III

Landmark judicial rulings shaped RTE implementation: the 2012 Society for Unaided Private Schools judgment upheld Section 12(1) (c) for private non-minority schools; the 2014 Pramati decision exempted minority institutions; and the Environmental & Consumer Protection Foundation case mandated basic drinking water and functional toilet infrastructure across all schools.

questions.question_english: What is the most appropriate reason the RTE Act emphasizes that the medium of instruction shall, as far as practicable, be in the child's mother tongue?
options_english: To enhance comprehension without language barriers hindering cognitive growth.
To actively discourage and minimize the learning and usage of English in primary and upper primary schools.
To significantly reduce the financial expenditure incurred by the state in printing textbooks across multiple languages.
To strictly comply with international bilateral language treaties and global educational recommendations.
questions.explanation_english: Section 29(2)(f) emphasizes mother-tongue instruction because learning in a familiar language accelerates early cognitive development, conceptual understanding, and self-expression. Eliminating language barriers in foundational years prevents academic exclusion, builds confidence, and fosters natural comprehension, ensuring that medium of instruction supports rather than hinders holistic learning processes.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर विकल्प A है। परिचित भाषा में सीखने से बच्चे को अवधारणाएँ समझने, प्रश्न पूछने और अपने विचार व्यक्त करने में मदद मिलती है। मातृभाषा में शिक्षण का उद्देश्य अंग्रेज़ी या अन्य भाषाओं को हतोत्साहित करना नहीं है, बल्कि यह सुनिश्चित करना है कि भाषा स्वयं अधिगम में अनावश्यक बाधा न बने। मुद्रण लागत या अंतरराष्ट्रीय संधियाँ इस प्रावधान का मुख्य शैक्षिक औचित्य नहीं हैं।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) To enhance comprehension without language barriers hindering cognitive growth.

Section 29(2)(f) emphasizes mother-tongue instruction because learning in a familiar language accelerates early cognitive development, conceptual understanding, and self-expression. Eliminating language barriers in foundational years prevents academic exclusion, builds confidence, and fosters natural comprehension, ensuring that medium of instruction supports rather than hinders holistic learning processes.

questions.question_english: Which of the following is NOT a defined category of schools under Section 2(n) of the RTE Act, 2009?
options_english: A school established, owned or controlled by the appropriate Government
An aided school receiving aid or grants from the appropriate Government
A recognized unaided school not receiving any kind of aid or grants
An unregistered home-schooling cooperative
questions.explanation_english: Section 2(n) defines four distinct categories of schools: government-established schools, government-aided schools receiving state grants, specified category schools such as Kendriya Vidyalayas, and recognized private unaided schools. Unregistered home-schooling cooperatives or informal home groups do not fall under any recognized category defined within the statutory framework, as formal recognition and standards are mandatory for educational operations.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर विकल्प D है। धारा 2(न) विद्यालयों की वैधानिक श्रेणियाँ बताती है, जिनमें सरकार द्वारा स्थापित या नियंत्रित विद्यालय, सहायता-प्राप्त विद्यालय, निर्दिष्ट श्रेणी के विद्यालय और मान्यता-प्राप्त गैर-सहायता-प्राप्त विद्यालय शामिल हैं। अपंजीकृत घरेलू-शिक्षण सहकारी समूह धारा 2(न) में अलग वैधानिक श्रेणी के रूप में सूचीबद्ध नहीं है। यहाँ ‘मान्यता’ और ‘सरकारी सहायता’ को अलग अवधारणाओं के रूप में समझना आवश्यक है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (D) An unregistered home-schooling cooperative

Section 2(n) defines four distinct categories of schools: government-established schools, government-aided schools receiving state grants, specified category schools such as Kendriya Vidyalayas, and recognized private unaided schools. Unregistered home-schooling cooperatives or informal home groups do not fall under any recognized category defined within the statutory framework, as formal recognition and standards are mandatory for educational operations.

questions.question_english: Which of the following statements is correct regarding the prohibition of private tuition under Section 28 of the RTE Act?
options_english: It prohibits all teachers from engaging in private tuition or private teaching activity.
It applies only to government school teachers; private school teachers can undertake tuitions.
Teachers can take private tuition if they obtain permission from the Principal.
Tuitions are allowed if they are provided free of cost to weaker sections.
questions.explanation_english: Section 28 explicitly provides that no teacher shall engage in private tuition or private teaching activity. This statutory ban applies universally to all school teachers, preventing conflict of interest, commercialization of education, and potential neglect of regular classroom teaching duties in both public and private institutions.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर विकल्प A है। धारा 28 के अनुसार शिक्षक निजी ट्यूशन या निजी शिक्षण गतिविधि में संलग्न नहीं हो सकते। यह प्रतिबंध केवल सरकारी विद्यालय के शिक्षकों तक सीमित नहीं है। प्रधानाचार्य की अनुमति या विद्यार्थियों से शुल्क न लेने जैसी शर्तें इस वैधानिक प्रतिबंध को स्वतः समाप्त नहीं करतीं। इसका उद्देश्य यह भी है कि शिक्षक नियमित कक्षा-शिक्षण को निजी ट्यूशन से जोड़कर विद्यार्थियों पर दबाव न डालें।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) It prohibits all teachers from engaging in private tuition or private teaching activity.

Section 28 explicitly provides that no teacher shall engage in private tuition or private teaching activity. This statutory ban applies universally to all school teachers, preventing conflict of interest, commercialization of education, and potential neglect of regular classroom teaching duties in both public and private institutions.

questions.question_english: What was the primary cause for the Central Government to grant a relaxation in the minimum qualifications for teachers under Section 23(2) during the initial years of the RTE Act's implementation?
options_english: To give states lacking training institutions time for recruits to acquire qualifications.
To significantly reduce the overall recurring financial and salary burden on various state education departments.
To actively encourage untrained fresh university graduates without B.Ed. or D.El.Ed degrees to permanently enter the teaching profession.
To permanently bypass and override the strict professional teacher qualification regulations set by the NCTE.
questions.explanation_english: Section 23(2) empowered the Central Government to relax minimum qualification standards for up to five years in states lacking adequate teacher training institutions. This temporary relaxation enabled states to recruit necessary teaching staff to meet Pupil-Teacher Ratios while providing recruits a transitional period to acquire mandatory professional qualifications.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर विकल्प A है। प्रारंभिक कार्यान्वयन के समय कुछ राज्यों में आवश्यक संख्या में योग्य शिक्षक और प्रशिक्षण संस्थान उपलब्ध नहीं थे। धारा 23(2) के अंतर्गत दी गई छूट का उद्देश्य ऐसी परिस्थितियों में संक्रमणकालीन व्यवस्था बनाना था, ताकि नियुक्त शिक्षक निर्धारित अवधि में आवश्यक न्यूनतम योग्यताएँ प्राप्त कर सकें। यह व्यवस्था शिक्षक-योग्यता मानकों को स्थायी रूप से समाप्त करने या केवल खर्च घटाने के लिए नहीं थी।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) To give states lacking training institutions time for recruits to acquire qualifications.

Section 23(2) empowered the Central Government to relax minimum qualification standards for up to five years in states lacking adequate teacher training institutions. This temporary relaxation enabled states to recruit necessary teaching staff to meet Pupil-Teacher Ratios while providing recruits a transitional period to acquire mandatory professional qualifications.
